name: Russia–NATO
value: Russian drone in Polish airspace 22 Nov
summary: Poland says a Russian drone entered its airspace deliberately on 22 Nov, after missiles fell there 20 Nov; no Article 4
state: A Russian drone briefly entered Polish airspace over the Lublin region late on 22 Nov during an attack on western Ukraine; Polish forces were cleared to shoot it down but let it leave as it turned east (Kyiv Independent). Poland's defence ministry said it believes the incursion was deliberate (Ukrainska Pravda, 24 Nov). It follows Russian missiles falling in eastern Poland on 20 Nov, reported violations in Moldova and Finland on 21 Nov, and Russia's 23 Nov warning to Estonia of open war. No Article 4 request or direct clash was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: Residents of eastern Poland and the Baltic states should follow alerts from their national civil protection authorities. Repeated incursions raise the chance of temporary airspace closures and flight disruption on NATO's eastern flank.
rubric_hit: Watch: airspace violations (Russian drone in Poland 22 Nov, missiles 20 Nov) and explicit threats against Estonia; no Article 4 or clash for Alert

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
